blocks.title: What you'll learn
objectives: Describe what happens when someone visits a website
Identify the roles of browsers, servers, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Explain why web pages are built from structured files

blocks.title: The request journey
blocks.body:
When you type a web address into your browser, the browser sends a request over the internet to a computer called a server. The server responds with files that describe the page. Your browser reads those files and turns them into the page you see.

Most pages use three core languages:
- **HTML** defines the structure and content
- **CSS** controls layout and visual style
- **JavaScript** adds interactivity

You do not need to memorize every detail yet. The important idea is that a website is a conversation between a browser and a server, using structured files.

code.content:
Browser  --request-->  Server
Browser  <--files---  Server
Browser renders HTML + CSS + JavaScript

blocks.question: Which statement best describes what a browser does when you visit a website?

options.label: It stores the website permanently on your computer before showing anything
It requests page files from a server and renders them into a visible page
It writes JavaScript directly onto the server hard drive

blocks.explanation: Browsers request files from servers and render HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into the page you see.

blocks.body: You now understand the basic request-and-render loop behind every website. Next you will write your first real HTML page and learn how structure turns into something people can read in the browser.
